clue.text: Joins together, yet finally splits on the outside

indicators.note: the splitting word sits around the other piece, wrapping it on both sides

parts.note: to rive is to split or tear apart

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the closing letter of yet

explanation.surface: A paradox: something that joins things together while also splitting them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten metal plates with pins, so the verb in the third person means fastens.

clue.text: Reduced time for part of army operation

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a mission is a military operation

explanation.surface: A shortened term of service granted for taking part in a military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Remission is the shortening of a prison sentence for good behaviour; RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is a cut in a prisoner's sentence, so it is a shortened stay behind bars.

clue.text: It might be a trap for a medium

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage, one example of a conveyance
second meaning: a means or channel of expression

explanation.surface: Something that could be a snare set for a spiritualist.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap is not a snare but a pony-drawn cart, and medium is not a psychic but a channel of communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle is any conveyance such as a cart, and also the means by which something is expressed.

clue.text: Duke of Milan and Duchess of Malfi, for example

definitions.text: Duke of Milan and Duchess of Malfi, for example

parts.words: Duke of Milan and Duchess of Malfi
parts.note: surface reading: two Italian aristocrats
setter's reading: both are characters who give their names to Jacobean plays, by Massinger and Webster

explanation.surface: Two Italian nobles cited as examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Milan is a play by Philip Massinger and The Duchess of Malfi one by John Webster; each lead character names the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts for which a drama is named are its leading characters, so each noble is the eponymous part.

clue.text: Outstanding success with a couple of shots

wordplay.note: two strokes in a ball game: a smash and a hit

explanation.surface: A triumph achieved with just two shots, as in a quick win at tennis or a shoot-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a show, record or film that proves an enormous popular triumph.

clue.text: Notable courtship combined hearts, perhaps

parts.note: major means important or notable
to pay suit to someone is to court them

explanation.surface: A memorable romance that joined two hearts together.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts are a card suit, not lovers' hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, spades and hearts are the higher-scoring suits, so hearts is an example of the higher-ranked pair.

clue.text: Type either of the letters right in front you, say

wordplay.words: either of the letters right in front you, say
wordplay.note: you sounds like U; the letters directly before U in the alphabet are S and T

explanation.surface: An instruction to key in one of the characters right before your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You, say' is the letter U; read 'either of' as the words S OR T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or category of thing, so it is a noun synonym for kind.

clue.text: Regular visitor somewhat put in the shade

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: A frequent caller rather overshadowed by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the shade' reads as one idiom meaning outshone, but it splits into an insertion instruction and a colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is someone who frequents a particular place, such as a regular at a bar.

clue.text: Statesman's article used in next broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's piece of writing being used in the next transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: Statesman is read as a man from a US state; Texas is the Lone Star State.
explanation.definitionFit: A Texan is a native of Texas, literally a man of an American state, so the clue's word fits.

clue.text: Tables, perhaps, brought up at short notice

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
ad is the shortened form of advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: Tables raised as a matter with little warning.
explanation.walkthrough: AT plus AD gives ATAD, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, and tables of numbers are one example of such information.

clue.text: Mother carrying headgear for Indian sage

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an affectionate word for mother
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A mother wearing a hat on behalf of a wise man from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a revered holy person or great soul, as given to Gandhi.

clue.text: Religious group said to fight in part of court

indicators.note: said means we go by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Jewry, the Jewish people as a whole, is pronounced the same as the word for a panel of jurors
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A sect reportedly getting into a brawl inside a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The jury box is the enclosed seating area of a courtroom where jurors sit during a trial.

clue.text: Piece of furniture to hide? Look inside

indicators.note: inside says one word is placed within the other

parts.note: to secrete something is to hide it away
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a cabinet is for hiding things, and told to peek in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nudges toward a secret drawer, but 'Look' is a noun for an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with drawers and a fold-down front, a cabinet-like item for the home.

clue.text: Place in Berkshire for point-to-point

parts.note: East, a point of the compass
taken as written
North, another compass point

explanation.surface: A town that hosts a point-to-point, a British cross-country horse race over fences.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase; here it is read literally as one compass point, the word to, then another.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a town on the Thames opposite Windsor, famous for its public school.

clue.text: Signal to renew fighting, slightly mistimed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the boxing call before a round, telling the corner men to leave the ring
second meaning: off by a matter of moments

explanation.surface: A bell for the next round that rings a little late.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the referee's call clearing the ring before a bout restarts, and literally says a clock is off by moments.

clue.text: Cod that is caught left out for freezing

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
i.e., Latin id est, means that is
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fish landed and left lying out until it freezes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-cold is an adjective for something chilled right through, as cold as frozen water.

clue.text: Record our Home Counties address

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
taken as written
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England

explanation.surface: A recording of the speech from our part of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal speech or lecture, the noun sense of an address given to an audience.

clue.text: Futile way to economise on supplies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pointless, of no avail
second meaning, read as two words: consume a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A grumble that cutting back on stock is a pointless exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it becomes the advice for making supplies last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile is pointless and serves no purpose, which is exactly what the adjective means.

clue.text: Firm set out advertisement quickly

indicators.note: out suggests disordered, so the preceding word's letters are shuffled

parts.note: the word set, rearranged
ad is short for advertisement
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A company quickly arranged for a commercial to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company noun but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast describes someone resolute and unwavering, which is the adjective sense of firm.

clue.text: Contemporary style seen in various quarters

wordplay.note: a string of compass points, the four quarters: North, East, West, North, East, South, South

explanation.surface: A modern fashion spotted all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are the compass points N, E, S and W; seven of them in the right order spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Newness is the quality of being recent or novel, the state of being up to date.

clue.text: Fish in can consumed by political type

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a Whig was a member of the historic British liberal party
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tinned fish eaten by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were the forerunners of the Liberal Party in British politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiting is a small sea fish of the cod family, common in European waters.

clue.text: In West End, foreign money can be a nuisance

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that letter of West is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of West
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: In London's theatre district, foreign currency is a bother to tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatreland, but here it means just the end of the word West.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a noun for bother or difficulty, something that annoys, matching a nuisance.

clue.text: Arrangement of locks in centre of industry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall dome-shaped hairdo
second meaning: the home of busy insects, a byword for hard work

explanation.surface: A layout of canal locks in an industrial hub.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are hair, not canal gates or door fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is a 1960s piled-up hairstyle, and a hive is a place full of busy activity.

clue.text: Leave out the captain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: omit or pass over
second meaning: informal word for a ship's master or team leader

explanation.surface: An instruction to exclude the team leader from the side.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to omit, and skip is also a short form of skipper, the person in charge of a team or boat.

clue.text: Capital I invested in furniture

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money placed into a fund

parts.note: a sofa is a piece of furniture
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has put their money into home furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money to be invested, but it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital here means a city that seats a national government; Sofia holds that role for Bulgaria.

clue.text: Catherine losing her head in novel

parts.note: Catherine Howard, Henry VIII's fifth wife, in the possessive
she was beheaded in 1542, so this was her end

explanation.surface: A queen's beheading as told in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Howard was executed for adultery; her death is literally the title of E. M. Forster's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Howards End is a 1910 novel by E. M. Forster about class in Edwardian England.

clue.text: Dispenses with alliances' choppers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gets rid of, cuts
second meaning: tools for cutting wood

explanation.surface: Someone getting rid of the helicopters belonging to some coalitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Alliances' slips in a third sense, the Axes as plural of axis, as in the wartime Axis powers. Choppers suggests helicopters but means cutting tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Axes are tools for felling trees, and to axe something is to cancel or remove it.

clue.text: Scattered keys forming part of island group

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keys dropped all over a little island chain, like the Florida Keys.
explanation.walkthrough: Keys also means low islands, which makes the surface feel like a geography clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, the chain off western Scotland.

clue.text: Film with hesitation in unsteady light

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a movie
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A movie shown with pauses under a wavering lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A flicker is a brief wavering burst of light, as from a candle in a draught.

clue.text: Blue material girl has to put back inside

indicators.note: inside means the turned word is placed within the name

parts.note: a girl's name

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written, with put as part of the instruction

explanation.surface: A young woman must replace some saucy literature on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue here means sexually explicit, not the colour or sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually explicit writing or art, and blue is the British slang adjective for smutty content.

clue.text: Island backing agreement on fish

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word before it is sent second in the answer

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: An island that supports a deal over fishing rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is a large island off the north-west coast of Wales, across the Menai Strait.

clue.text: Way in which the average man can be found

definitions.text: Way in which the average man can be found

parts.words: Way in which the average man can be found
parts.note: surface reading: a method for tracking down a typical person
setter's reading: the ordinary person is proverbially the man in a particular public thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A method for locating an ordinary, typical person.
explanation.walkthrough: Way is a road, not a method; the phrase 'the man in the street' means the average citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, and the idiom names it as home of the typical citizen.
